summary: Climate change mitigation efforts are crucial for reducing greenhouse gas emissions. This project measures the real power draw and carbon emissions of software applications, enabling businesses and consumers to accurately assess emissions at an individual software level. The initiative aims to provide a greater level of granularity in reporting, facilitating more effective climate action. The project's methodology involves collecting energy consumption data, mapping applications to devices, and attributing power to these applications. The calculated energy consumption is then converted to emission figures, considering location-based and market-based emission factors. This approach is designed for reporting Scope 2 emissions under the GHG Protocol, supporting efforts to reduce energy-related emissions and mitigate climate change. The project's focus on software carbon emissions makes it relevant to the global effort to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and transition to a low-carbon economy.
